extracted.intended_audience: corporate investor relations officers, investor relations counselors, corporate communications officers, general counsel, CFOs and boards of publicly traded companies
extracted.subtask_description: Standards of practice and guidelines for corporate investor relations (IROs and counselors) covering disclosure policy, communications with the investment community and media, Regulation FD and G compliance, earnings communications, analyst relations, insider trading policies and professional ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral participant in corporate strategy / need to know
rubrics_metrics.description: To be effective, the investor relations officer has a 'need to know' and, therefore, must have full access to senior management and, preferably, a seat at the table with senior management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full access enables the IRO to speak authoritatively and credibly about strategic direction and prospects. Knowledge of strategy, budgets, forecasts and contemplated developments does not mean disclosure will occur at will; disclosure only upon authorization and in line with the company’s disclosure policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization required for disclosure of strategic/forward-looking matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of strategy, budgets, forecasts and other developments will be done only upon authorization of the company’s CEO or other senior officer with responsibility in this area and in line with the company’s disclosure policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spokespersons must not discuss such subjects except when authorized; knowledge alone does not permit disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarity with company disclosure record
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone in a spokesperson role must be completely familiar with the company’s record of disclosure in order to guard against unauthorized disclosures of material, nonpublic information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ignorance is not an excuse (SEC v. Carnation). IROs should accompany senior officials in meetings and listen in on calls to detect inadvertent disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompany senior officials to avoid inadvertent disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: To detect inadvertent disclosure of material, nonpublic information or to avoid potentially intentional disclosure of such information, the IRO should accompany senior officials in meetings with analysts and investors and listen in on telephone calls between senior officials and analysts or investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inadvertent disclosure occurs, the company must issue a news release within 24 hours of when the official became aware or before the next trading day, whichever is later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility through correction and timely updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Credibility comes not only from knowledge but from a demonstrated willingness to correct or update changes in information on a timely basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to correct/update timely may cause long-term or irreparable damage to management and the spokesperson’s credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of accurate, complete and transparent information
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical to the marketing process is the provision of accurate, complete and transparent information about the company, along with a duty to update that information when material changes occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materiality defined broadly as information that in the total mix would cause a reasonable investor to make an investment decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level playing field / fair and impartial access
rubrics_metrics.description: The IRO is responsible for assuring a 'level playing field' for investors by providing information on a fair and impartial basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differential disclosure is permissible for nonmaterial information but must not withhold material nonpublic information from other investors, analysts or the media when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differential disclosure — caution against selective disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Differential disclosure may become a form of selective disclosure, detrimental if a company gives analysts/institutional investors greater supporting detail yet refuses the same information to reporters or the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious that differential disclosure does not evolve into selective disclosure; ensure fairness and access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing market intelligence to senior management and the board
rubrics_metrics.description: IROs should play a key role providing market intelligence to senior management and the board for use in strategic decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Market intelligence includes analyst and investor comments, competitor information, market research and monitoring shareholder mix and investment styles to determine desired shareholder mix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep senior management apprised of publicly disclosed information
rubrics_metrics.description: Keeping senior management apprised of the company’s disclosure record is a very important function for the IRO, particularly with the adoption of Reg FD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IROs should keep records of all public disclosures, train/brief spokespersons on what has or has not been publicly released, and promote consistent one-voice communications among management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to correct in a timely manner (legal duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: As a matter of law, companies have a duty to correct material information that they believed was correct when first disclosed but is later determined to be incorrect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use news releases, fully accessible webcasts or SEC filings to correct. Failure can lead to liability (Ross v. A. H. Robins Co.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to update in a timely manner (best practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: A duty to update occurs where information was correct when disclosed but subsequently there is a material change; update public information on material changes in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law is weaker than for duty to correct, but timely updates are good investor relations practice and good business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate disclosure policy should be written and reflect commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete disclosure policy represents a public company’s commitment to full, fair and consistent disclosure and to maintain realistic investor expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy should be a policy document, not an operational 'how-to'; overly specific operational steps risk being used in litigation if deviated from. A written disclosure policy and insider-trading policy may lower D&O insurance costs and be relevant under Reg FD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure policy decisions on voluntary disclosure and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: When developing a disclosure policy, a key question is how much corporate information beyond SEC requirements should be volunteered, particularly how much earnings guidance will be provided and in what forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how guidance will be updated during the quarter and avoid boilerplate risk-factor warnings when using the safe harbor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a disclosure committee with specified minimum membership
rubrics_metrics.description: NIRI believes the disclosure committee should, at a minimum, consist of the senior IRO, the controller, the general counsel and the chief corporate communications officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee reviews SEC filings and news releases, reacts to developments requiring materiality and timing decisions, and provides guidance rather than conduct IR activities 'by committee.' CFO inclusion varies by matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the Safe Harbor for Forward-Looking Information
rubrics_metrics.description: The safe harbor under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act protects companies that make good-faith forward-looking statements if investors are adequately warned of the most likely potential risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies should disclose risk factors specific to forecasts (not boilerplate). In oral statements, refer to written documents for risk factors; consider archiving webcasts/transcripts. Don’t use safe harbor warnings where no forward-looking statements exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is not covered by the Safe Harbor
rubrics_metrics.description: The safe harbor does not cover forward-looking statements made in conjunction with an IPO, tender offer, Section 13(d) disclosure, going-private or roll-up transaction; additionally, financial statements are not covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is considered a forward-looking statement (enumeration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projections of revenues, income, EPS, capex, dividends, capital structure or other financial items; management’s plans or objectives for future operations; plans or objectives for products/services; statements relating to future economic performance; MD&A information in 10-K/10-Q; any statements of assumptions underlying the above; any report by an outside reviewer assessing forward-looking statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion and voluntary disclosure of nonfinancial performance factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should consider discussing nonfinancial performance measures (intangibles) with analysts and investors as these can be significant in valuing a corporation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most nonfinancial measures cannot be audited but remain important; companies are encouraged to volunteer information on intangible assets and management quality, and expose senior managers periodically to the investment community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination: structured vs unstructured disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Information filed with the SEC (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K) is 'structured disclosure'; glossy annual reports, news releases, speeches, web site, conference calls and meetings are 'unstructured disclosure.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How information is disseminated and under what conditions is governed by SEC regulations and listing-exchange disclosure sections; Reg G and Sarbanes-Oxley affect some unstructured disclosures (e.g., furnishing news releases on 8-K).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information dissemination methods should meet SEC/listed-exchange standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted means for accomplishing full public dissemination are contained in SEC regulations and listed-company manuals published by NYSE, Nasdaq and AMEX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of furnishing requirements (e.g., Form 8-K) and Reg G website posting obligations for certain non-GAAP information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insider trading policy for senior management and directors
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior managers and directors are insiders under Section 16; trades must be filed with the SEC within 48 hours and posted on the company’s Web site; insiders may not trade while in possession of material, nonpublic information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies typically establish trading windows opened after full public disclosure; compliance officer (general counsel or corporate secretary) should approve Section 16 filers’ trades and close windows when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicating with nonmanagement employee shareholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should treat employee shareholders (non-Section 16 insiders) cautiously — provide either fully public information or nonmaterial nonpublic information, and consider providing a digest or representative sample of analyst reports but avoid disseminating analyst reports broadly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disseminating analyst reports to nonemployee investors is strongly discouraged as it may imply company endorsement and create litigation risk; employees briefed on material nonpublic information must be advised they are insiders and must not trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investor relations counselors: professionalism obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Counselors should practice to provide the highest level of knowledge, expertise and value-added services, exercise professionalism, serve the public interest, adhere to laws, and maintain capital markets integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counselors must balance public interests with client interests and place those above their own, exercising integrity, objectivity and due care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counselor competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Counselors should diligently discharge responsibilities, render services promptly, carefully and thoroughly, and comply with applicable technical, legal and ethical standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If engagement exceeds a counselor’s competence, the counselor should recommend a specialist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counselor objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Counselors should exercise independent professional judgment in assisting clients and placing public interest over self-interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Counselors should avoid relationships that might affect, or be perceived to affect, their ethical practice of investor relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure and management of conflicts are implied; the counselor must place client and public interests above personal gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representing the client company ethically (no stock promotion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counselors must represent client companies and not engage in stock-promotion activities; promoting micro- and small-cap stocks in conjunction with boiler-room tactics is not condoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investor relations that amount to stock promotion are improper and not supported by NIRI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic and tactical services — value to clients
rubrics_metrics.description: Counselors should provide strategic and tactical investor relations services consistent with professional standards and add value to clients’ goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services and fee arrangements should demonstrate professionalism consistent with NIRI standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation transparency and professionalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Counselors should enter into fee arrangements and offer services in a manner demonstrating professionalism consistent with NIRI Standards of Practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees and services should reflect professional excellence and avoid impropriety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality of information (disclosure guideline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Materiality: information that taken within the total mix of information would cause a reasonable investor to make an investment decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materiality considerations drive disclosure decisions; guidance expanded elsewhere in the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of material information
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must disclose material information using news releases, fully accessible webcasts or SEC filings to ensure timely, complete, accurate and transparent disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid excessive delays disclosing negative information; ensure accessibility and full public dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussing public information
rubrics_metrics.description: When discussing public information, IROs should ensure accuracy and context and avoid implying undisclosed material information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful in commentary and avoid leading statements that could be construed as selective disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mosaic information
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of mosaic information (assembling public, nonmaterial information into insight) is permissible as long as it does not reveal material, nonpublic information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on material nonpublic pieces; ensure mosaic does not cross into selective disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distributing or referring to analysts’ reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should be cautious when distributing or referring to analysts’ reports; distributing full analyst reports to investors is discouraged because it may imply company endorsement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate to provide a complete listing of analysts who follow the company; avoid broad dissemination of analyst reports to nonemployees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with rumors or leaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should have procedures for dealing with rumors or leaks; respond appropriately and consider issuing clarifying information when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid speculation; evaluate materiality and timing and use news releases or SEC filings for corrective information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to rumors or inquiries regarding a possible earnings decline
rubrics_metrics.description: When asked about potential earnings declines or responding to rumors, companies should assess whether information is material and follow disclosure procedures to correct or update as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If material and inadvertently disclosed, follow Reg FD timing (news release within 24 hours) and internal disclosure committee procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quiet period guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies may adopt quiet periods around earnings releases or other events during which they limit comments about results to avoid selective disclosure or guidance confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quiet period practices vary; ensure consistent application and disclosure policy alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondisclosure briefings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nondisclosure briefings (private briefings) should be handled with caution to avoid selective disclosure of material information; ensure information shared is nonmaterial or made public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document briefings and consider contemporaneous public dissemination if material information is disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing material information to reporters on an exclusive basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing material information to reporters on an exclusive basis risks selective disclosure and is discouraged unless matched by public dissemination to satisfy Reg FD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If material information is provided exclusively, the company must make public disclosure consistent with Reg FD timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to correct / duty to update material changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies have a duty to correct material misstatements and to update material changes in information; timely public corrections and updates are expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use news releases, webcasts or SEC filings; failure can lead to loss of credibility or legal liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of technology and internet for dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Internet and technology (webcasts, archiving, push e-mail) is appropriate for dissemination but does not substitute for news releases required by Reg FD/SEC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archive teleconferences/webcasts and transcripts; push e-mail may be used to notify opt-in investors but is not a substitute for news releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference call practices and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference calls should be announced in advance; web site access is sufficient; calls may be listen-only; IRO and CFO should participate and CEO/other senior management regularly or periodically participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If new material information is disclosed on a call, include it in earnings press release or subsequent news release; if inadvertent disclosure occurs, issue news release or furnish/file 8-K within Reg FD timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-on-one meetings guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: One-on-one meetings are not public events; oral comments in one-on-one settings are generally not subject to reconciliation requirements for non-GAAP measures, but care must be taken not to disclose material nonpublic information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document what is discussed; avoid disclosure of material nonpublic facts unless simultaneously publicized as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities of analysts who receive material, nonpublic information
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysts who receive material nonpublic information have responsibilities (implied) to refrain from trading on it and to respect confidentiality; companies should manage access and documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish policies governing analyst access, review of draft reports, and procedures to avoid selective disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to information and corporate management (analyst relations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on access to management: companies should control access carefully, ensure equal access, and avoid selective disclosure when interacting with analysts/investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider structured access, documented meetings, and consistent messages; allow one-on-one access but manage material information risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of draft analyst reports/models
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should have procedures regarding review of draft analyst reports or models, mindful that review may raise issues of selective disclosure or implied endorsement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious in commenting on draft analyst work; avoid endorsing or materially altering analyst conclusions without public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance regarding analyst conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for analysts: avoid conflicts, disclose relationships, and maintain independence; issuers should not unduly influence analyst reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuer-paid research and gifts/trips are addressed to avoid conflicts and perception of undue influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuer-paid research — caution and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuer-paid research should be handled carefully to avoid conflicts of interest and the appearance of compromised analyst independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish clear policies, disclosure and appropriate compensation terms; be transparent with investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company-sponsored trips for analysts and investors — policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Company-sponsored trips should be governed by policies to avoid inappropriate gifts or inducements to analysts and investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit content to informational activities, document agendas, and avoid lavish perks; consider compliance and disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company gifts for analysts and investors — avoid improper gifts
rubrics_metrics.description: Gifts to analysts and investors should be modest and comply with ethical standards to avoid perceived influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have written policies defining acceptable gifts and disclosure practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earnings conference calls and webcasts: announcement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is a scheduled event (e.g., investor conference presentation), announce it in advance using acceptable methods so it can satisfy Reg FD requirements for full disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An announcement that a call will be held without reason may cause speculation; include reason in press release for major webcast events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earnings call accessibility and 48-hour rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If an earnings release is issued and a conference call is held within 48 hours, furnishing the earnings release on an 8-K prior to the call lets the company avoid furnishing the transcript after the call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria: call complementary to and within 48 hours of release; release furnished on 8-K prior to call; call properly noticed and fully accessible; presentation materials and Reg G reconciliation posted on web site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation G — applicability and SEC focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Reg G applies to disclosures of material information that include non-GAAP measures and the SEC is particularly concerned about use of non-GAAP financial information in earnings releases and compliance with Reg G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reconciliation of non-GAAP measures to most directly comparable GAAP measure and provide detailed, non-boilerplate explanations of why the measure is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation G — reconcile non-GAAP to most comparable GAAP measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must reconcile non-GAAP measures (e.g., EBITDA) to the most directly comparable GAAP measure(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconcile to net income and/or cash flow as appropriate; if using non-GAAP as liquidity measure, reconcile to cash flow; if as performance measure, reconcile to net income. If reconciliation unavailable without unreasonable effort, disclose that fact and probable significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg G — reconciling forward-looking non-GAAP measures
rubrics_metrics.description: If giving a non-GAAP measure for forward-looking information, the reconciliation requirement still applies unless the reconciling information is not available without unreasonable effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reconciliation unavailable, identify unavailable information and disclose probable significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg G — web posting and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Reg G information and reconciliation should be posted on the company’s Web site (investor relations section) and the SEC suggests keeping it there for one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No strict rule on location, but follow SEC guidance for accessibility and retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg G — oral vs public presentation reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral statements in one-on-one presentations need not be reconciled since such presentations are not public events; public webcasts and conference calls using non-GAAP require reconciliation and web posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure public events are accompanied by reconciliation information posted on the Web site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg G — 48-hour exemption criteria (summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid filing an 8-K with a call transcript, the company must: conduct a fully accessible call within 48 hours of the earnings release; furnish the earnings release on an 8-K prior to the call; properly notice the call and accessibility; and post financial and reconciliation info on the Web site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting these criteria avoids additional 8-Ks for transcripts but still requires compliance with Reg G posting and notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for improving quality of earnings announcements — include financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Earnings announcements should, at a minimum, include both a complete income statement and a complete balance sheet; preferably a statement of cash flows should also be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include current quarter, prior-year quarter, and if informative sequential quarter data; balance sheet comparisons to current period and prior fiscal year-end; enables investors to determine free cash flow and liquidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earnings announcements — put GAAP earnings first
rubrics_metrics.description: Put GAAP earnings up front and before pro forma results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Reg G requirements for non-GAAP presentation and avoid misleading prominence of non-GAAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earnings announcements — include key MD&A-type information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include additional information investors need to evaluate results — either include a summary MD&A with the earnings announcement or incorporate critical information into the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested items: brief business description; factors/trends driving revenues; drivers of gross profit, SG&A, interest, taxes; explanation of charges (pre- and after-tax); liquidity and capital resources discussion; key industry-specific performance measures; material accounting changes; current expectations/guidance if provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIRI Code of Ethics — maintain integrity and credibility (Regular members #1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain my integrity and credibility by practicing investor relations in accordance with the highest legal and ethical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIRI Code of Ethics — avoid appearance of impropriety (Regular #2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid even the appearance of professional impropriety in the conduct of my investor relations responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIRI Code of Ethics — support transparency of credible information (Regular #3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that the integrity of the capital markets is based on transparency of credible financial and nonfinancial corporate information, and will to the best of my ability and knowledge work to ensure that my company or client fully and fairly discloses this important information.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIRI Code of Ethics — provide fair access (Regular #4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide analysts, institutional and individual investors and the media fair access to corporate information.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIRI Code of Ethics — serve shareholders and stakeholders (Regular #5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Honor my obligation to serve the interest of shareholders and other stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIRI Code of Ethics — remain current on laws and affairs (Regular #6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discharge my responsibilities completely and competently by keeping myself abreast of the affairs of my company or client as well as the laws and regulations affecting the practice of investor relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIRI Code of Ethics — maintain confidentiality (Regular #7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain the confidentiality of information acquired in the course of my work for my company or client company.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIRI Code of Ethics — do not use confidential info for personal advantage (Regular #8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not use confidential information acquired in the course of my work for my personal advantage nor for the advantage of related parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIRI Code of Ethics — exercise independent professional judgment (Regular #9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise independent professional judgment in the conduct of my duties and responsibilities on behalf of my company or client.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIRI Code of Ethics — avoid professional relationships that affect ethics (Regular #10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid any professional/business relationships that might affect, or be perceived to potentially affect, my ethical practice of investor relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIRI Code of Ethics — report suspected fraud or illegality (Regular #11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report to appropriate company authorities if I suspect or recognize fraudulent or illegal acts within the company.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIRI Code of Ethics — represent profession reputably (Regular #12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent myself in a reputable and dignified manner that reflects the professional stature of investor relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate Member Code of Ethics — maintain integrity (Associate #1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain my integrity and credibility as I provide service and support to my investor relations clients in accordance with the highest legal and ethical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate Member Code of Ethics — stay current on relevant laws (Associate #2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep myself abreast of the laws and regulations affecting the practice of investor relations for my investor relations clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate Member Code of Ethics — maintain client confidentiality (Associate #3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain the confidentiality of information acquired in the course of my work for my investor relations clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate Member Code of Ethics — no use of confidential info for advantage (Associate #4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not use confidential information acquired in the course of my work for my personal advantage nor for the advantage of related parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate Member Code of Ethics — exercise independent judgment (Associate #5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise independent judgment in the conduct of my duties and responsibilities on behalf of clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate Member Code of Ethics — support clients' ethical IR practice (Associate #6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support my investor relations clients in their efforts to practice investor relations in an ethical manner.
